def: An agent that finds, reads, edits and runs code in a repository, using test and build results as feedback.
The set of commands and output formats an agent uses to work on a computer, designed for a model's strengths and weaknesses rather than a person's.
A file-reading tool that shows a fixed number of numbered lines at a time, keeping each observation small.
An edit expressed as exact old text and new text, which fails loudly if the old text is missing or appears more than once.
A check after an edit that rejects it if the file no longer parses, leaving the file unchanged and returning the error.
A compact summary of a repository's files and key signatures, sent with requests so the model knows what exists before searching.
A benchmark of 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories, graded by running the repository's tests on the agent's patch.
A subset of 500 SWE-bench instances that human developers screened for clear issue descriptions and fair tests.
The two test sets used to grade a patch: tests that must start passing, and tests that must keep passing.
An ordered log of every action an agent takes and every observation it receives, which makes runs replayable.
A Markdown file in a repository, such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, that tells a coding agent how to build, test and follow local conventions.
